## 9. Wave-19 identity retry and local production lifecycle

Commission: Charlie's day-two addendum, wave-19 fixes #6/#7 (2026-10-19).
This amends the SDK/proof and local release contracts; it grants no new auth
or filesystem authority. SEC4 and QRY keep their existing scopes.

Identity `guest`, `signup` and `login` share a portable request helper with
proof `seedAccounts` (including `startServe({seedUsers})`). Only a delivered
HTTP 429 containing a validated auth `E_RATE_LIMIT` refusal, not marked
`retryable:false`, may retry. The server refuses these requests before account
creation/authentication. Wait for nonnegative integer `retryAfterMs`, or a
valid Retry-After header on older servers (otherwise one second). Preserve the
same credentials and scope, without sending retry options on the wire. Up to
four attempts fit inside the whole request deadline (`timeoutMs`, default
180000); an AbortSignal cancels fetch and waiting. A wait that cannot fit
returns the original refusal with its delay; setup instead throws
E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, warning that partial accounts/grants may remain. Setup
passes its remaining overall budget (default five minutes). There is no
polling at a fixed short interval. Transport errors, malformed responses,
other status/family/codes, permanent refusals, session rotations and role
provisioning mutations never automatically replay. Account/role admission,
peer/email/KDF limits and the staging-before-mint boundary stay unchanged.
These deadlines rely on the fetch implementation honoring AbortSignal, as the
standard fetch does. Custom fetch adapters must honor that contract too.

Deploy and rollback may wait up to five seconds to acquire the actual owner
flock before admission. Missing/unreachable address hints select bounded
waiting; a responsive listener selects the existing authenticated control
status path. If that read-only status fails while shutdown is underway, use
only the remaining acquisition budget, then reread status under the acquired
owner. Neither status nor an address/PID hint admits activation. A subsequent
activation request or ambiguous reply is never replayed automatically. The
exclusive flock, canonical inode/hardlink checks, private auxiliary files,
revision CAS and immutable-source validation remain authoritative. Prune and
other offline command semantics are unchanged. A surviving owner still
refuses E_STORE_BUSY; no process is signalled based on a hint.

`serve DIR --wait-stopped` exposes a five-second lock-release barrier for
callers retaining their own process handle. It requires an existing database,
opens only its existing hardened private owner sidecar, obtains an exclusive
flock and validates the named sidecar/database inode. It does not open SQLite,
create a deployment/sidecar, clear address metadata or signal a PID. No owner
sidecar means no named ownership exclusion. The documented sidecar removal
boundary of LLP 3000.019 §3.4 remains; this is a point-in-time barrier, not a
reservation against a future owner. Other serve flags refuse before effects.

Proof `startServe().stop()` first terminates/reaps the retained native child
through the existing bounded TERM/KILL path, then awaits this barrier, including
any watchdog-held descriptor during worker cleanup. Concurrent/repeated stops
share the in-flight/successful operation. Failure rejects, clears the cached
failure and allows a later barrier retry; it cannot falsely claim cleanup.
No new PID lookup or automatic stop of another owner is introduced. The proof
host stop allowance includes the native child and five-second store barrier.

`data TABLE --json` returns `{rows, more, limit}` for empty and nonempty
snapshots, replacing the bare array. `more` reports the existing one-extra-row
probe in the same read transaction, including default 50-row truncation and
`--limit 0`. Text JSON-lines and the stderr notice are preserved. This operator
surface still bypasses application read rules and refuses private/ephemeral
storage as before; no query semantics change. Existing repository consumers
and the 0.4.35 guide changes are updated for the envelope.

Required evidence: SDK/seed refusal timing, bounded attempts, cancellation and
non-replay tests; actual owner wait/no-effect probes; real delayed worker stop;
deploy/rollback cleanup with a still-listening stale control hint; JSON default
and explicit limit boundaries. Fresh packed Linux qualification must include
real server throttles and public SDK/seedUsers retry, production shutdown and
stdout-only inspection; affected Mac Studio lifecycle tests cover platform
sensitivity. Final exact results, review provenance and scoped limitations are
recorded in WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md.

## 10. Wave-20 loop repairs (DX5)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-20 fix list #4, #6, #7, #8;
implementer Codex, 2026-10-21. This amendment is proposed until its two
independent reviews and implementation evidence are recorded. SEC5 owns
security intent, campaigns and exposure output; this lane changes lookup
advice, never the authority granted by an application rule.

### Clock reports

Amend LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4's proof helper return: `advance(duration)`
returns `{now, fired, held}`. Each entry carries the schedule name, target,
reason, boundary/window metadata and bounded run summary from the existing
operator-only schedule report. `now()` still returns a number. The CLI and
HTTP advance reply expose the same arrays, retaining `schedules` for existing
operator consumers. Fired means a schedule was enqueued, not that its job
succeeded; the run summary distinguishes parked or pending work. Every
non-fired schedule appears in held with a reason, including an already
processed boundary, a future saved boundary, initialization, a future window
or an explicit hold. Saved boundaries survive restart: one fire per boundary,
coalescing missed periods unless eachBoundary was explicitly requested.
The helper and CLI print saved-boundary holds and their recovery action on
stderr, including the equal-boundary case on a reused store. Advance never
rewinds markers or replays a completed boundary. Reply limits account for the
retained report plus its partition into fired/held. Staging's expiry notice
describes expiry/upload recovery without development-door instructions.
Ambiguous or failed advances are never retried; time may already have moved.
Maintenance failures return an explicitly incomplete schedule report with the
advanced time; the proof helper attaches this reply to its thrown error.

### Source diagnostics without an existence oracle

Extend LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2's N_LOOKUP_FILTERED advice to required reads
and reads of written tables. A later write and an asserted `! else CODE` do
not prove read authority. Existing key/flow proofs still suppress advice,
including prior successful exact reads and deliberately public projections.
One note names the source lookup, authored hiding rule, declaration and the
null/custom-refusal consequence; duplicate N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN notes at that
site are avoided (the more specific N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN takes precedence). This is missing-proof advice, not a claim every caller
is refused. Program `exists` and rule-witness `exists` keep distinct semantics.

For private tables with secondary unique keys, source advice explains that
an unreadable conflicting row uses generic E_RULE (or an undisclosed write
target miss), even when the unique declaration has `else CODE`. The named
constraint applies only when the conflict can be disclosed. Do not return
the declared code only on hidden conflicts: that would violate LLP 3000 §7
and LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2. Public E_RULE repair text, if changed, is identical
for ordinary rule rejection and hidden collision. No row, key, actual hiding
clause or hidden-dependent meter enters the public refusal. Rewrites propose
a minimal readable key projection or operator-mediated ownership/claim flow,
never broader disclosure of private rows. Paired hidden/missing lookup tests assert equality of public diagnostics and
logical meters. Hidden/ordinary write-refusal tests compare public refusals
and receipts; write replies expose no meter.

### Upgrade advice reaches the old CLI

Extend §8's bounded scan with candidate `data ... --json` consumers in authored
scripts, including argv-array and shell forms. List paths without printing
source. State the one-line migration `JSON.parse(stdout).rows` for the former
bare array, and preserve `more`/`limit`. This is a candidate scan, not an AST
proof or an automatic rewrite; report scan limits.

The installed wrapper runs project warnings before the first ordinary check
for that installed version, independently of the runtime-history receipt.
A warning receipt is written only after delivery to a terminal (or an empty
scan). Piped/captured stderr cannot establish delivery: old quiet upgrades
discard it, so a nonempty scan stays unacknowledged and the next ordinary
check repeats the advice, including in CI. Baseline checks neither deliver
nor acknowledge warnings; read/receipt failures do not fail compilation.
Warnings always use stderr, preserving one-object JSON stdout and quiet-mode
visibility. This reaches the usual published 0.4.33/0.4.35 upgrade path because
their upgrade invokes the newly installed wrapper for check. A fresh-process
resolution must select new bytes after package replacement. Direct upgrade
keeps its existing pre-install warning behavior. Test both published old CLIs
against the fresh packed package in an isolated local registry, including
--quiet and --json --quiet and the deferred first check; do not claim
an upgrade was tested by invoking only the new helper.

### Frontend and starter custody

Extend LLP 3000.013.002 §2 with `ReadState` in snapback4/react: a list read
(or PageHook) renders loading, denied, empty, or authorized data through one
component. It adds no subscription, cache or authority. It preserves partial
and stale rows; empty means the returned list is empty, never proven absence.
Loading and empty default to null; denied uses the supplied renderer or
throws the existing QueryRefusal for an error boundary. Children receive the
typed list and precise settled read metadata. Browser and React Native
callers supply their own display elements.

The Expo adapter owns `snapback4-expo/metro` (CommonJS withSnapback(config))
and its wasm transformer. Resolve Expo's transformer relative to the consuming
project/config, compatible with isolated package-manager installs. Preserve
the caller's config and append the existing .snapback4 block and wasm support.
New starter Metro config only obtains Expo's default and calls withSnapback.
The adapter also owns the native smoke sign-in hook; new starters import it
instead of carrying src/native-smoke.ts. Password and guest selection remain
explicit; ordinary launches never sign in automatically. Adapt removes a recognized old helper only when the planned source no longer
references it; custom references, modified helpers and unknown source symlinks
retain application custody. Old generated Metro prose remains recognizable
when adapting an untouched README. No native engine or simulator custody changes.

Amend LLP 3000.011.003.000 §7.2: adapt replaces an untouched todo frontend
proof with a runnable proof scaffold retaining frontend:proof/proof:web and
Playwright. It starts the correct frontend and checks rendered content, then
explicitly refuses to claim an app-specific write proof until the builder
adds one. A public schema without identity or personas skips sign-in and still
checks rendering before the missing-scenario refusal. A custom proof is never
rewritten. Fresh non-todo starters get the
same scaffold. Every Expo starter includes playwright-core, including custom
schemas. Qualification runs changed guide/starter sources from the packed
tarball, tests the expected scaffold refusal, and records frontend character
reductions on copies of three wave-20 Expo lanes. No original lane is edited.

### Acceptance and scope

## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.

### Session input and compatibility

Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.

### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries

ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.

For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
deadlines/backoffs remain business time.

Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
bearer's matching request URL/header, monotonically increases expiry/cap and
persists through existing credential/custody fences before clock listeners run.
Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
clock publication are serialized: durable local credential saves are awaited
before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
auth operation or remote revocation queue.
Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.

advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.

A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
schedule, saved boundary, next window and recovery duration. Fresh staging
storage and continuing with the original offset are recovery choices; saved
markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.

### Upgrade advice and future formats

Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
guide changes remains available. No ancestor
process inspection or script mutation is introduced.

The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.

### Starter and proof rendering

Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and
partial empty results retain distinct text, with existing freshness and
pagination semantics unchanged. Rename the docs' local ReadState example to
ReadNotice so it does not shadow the export. Password clients omit persona
selection and explicit web witness/generated API imports. The proof driver installs the
existing witness bridge before app creation; createApp calls an immutable Symbol observer only under explicit witness=web.
This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication
boundary. A witness URL alone installs no observer and exposes no App global.
The driver installs its nonconfigurable/nonwritable observer before application
scripts and locks/freezes the selected witness bridge; the first App remains
selected for that page. Same-App explicit API registration can enrich it;
a different explicit App refuses E_WITNESS_APP_SELECTION and requires a separate
page. Later automatic Apps cannot silently redirect the proof. Application JS
remains trusted to implement the application: same-origin code can forge its
own test observer outside a driven page, just as it can read web session storage.
The observer grants no new credentials or backend authority. Ordinary bundles
carry only the creation dispatch, not the witness implementation. No-API
registration captures only durable non-ephemeral mutation handles; direct
witness mutate still requires generated API.

Proof text locators match normalized entire descendant text, including composed
React Native spans and wrapping labels. Choose smallest matching visible,
non-editable elements; independent matches retain strict Playwright ambiguity.
Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,
with no Unicode normalization or input value matching. Exact strings are case-sensitive;
explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
Text ranges outside overflow clips do not contribute evidence to a visible
ancestor. Layoutless wrappers may forward their visible descendants; a clipped
suffix cannot manufacture a complete status label.

### Required evidence and review

Unit/HTTP/browser tests cover safe legacy input, seeded account sessions,
non-TTY warning receipts, fresh init, refusal tests, future formats, numeric
coercion, saved-boundary no-effect refusal, maintenance pause/resume and session
preservation versus explicit expiry. Execute changed guide snippets and all

# LLP 3000: Snapback 4 — the decided-substrates candidate

**Type:** Explainer
**Status:** Active
**Role:** Root of the Snapback 4 corpus (LLPs 3000 and up)
**Systems:** Everything under `snapback4/` once it exists; the bakeoff protocol shared with Snapback 3 (LLP 2000) and Snapback 2 (LLP 1000)
