    39	  estimatedServerNow = (): number => Math.min(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, Math.max(0, Math.round(this.wall() + this.offset)));
    40	  private deviceCandidate = (): number => Math.min(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, Math.max(0, Math.round(this.wall() + (this.issuedOffset ?? 0))));
    41	  /** Monotonic issued device time: execution, prediction, expiry and rendering. */
    42	  issuedDeviceNow = (): number => this.last = Math.max(this.last, this.deviceCandidate());
    43	  /** Adopt a committed admission without changing the server-time estimate. */
    44	  raiseIssued(time: number): void {
    45	    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(time) || time < 0 || time <= this.last) return;
    46	    const shift = time - Math.max(this.last, this.deviceCandidate());
    47	    this.last = time;
    48	    // Even a one-millisecond floor increase may cross a frozen deadline.
    49	    if (shift > 0) for (const listener of this.listeners) listener(shift, true);
    50	  }
    51	  subscribe = (listener: (shift: number, reschedule: boolean) => void): (() => void) => {
    52	    this.listeners.add(listener);
    53	    return () => { this.listeners.delete(listener); };
    54	  };
    55	  sample(serverNow: number, sent: number, received: number, revision?: string, order = ++this.order, provisional = false) {
    56	    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(serverNow) || serverNow < 0 || !Number.isFinite(sent) || !Number.isFinite(received) || received < sent) return;
    57	    this.order = Math.max(this.order, order);
    58	    const revisionChanged = revision !== undefined && revision !== this.revision;
    59	    if (revisionChanged) {
    60	      // A delayed reply from before an advance cannot restore the old window.
    61	      const split = (value: string) => value.split(":");
    62	      const [epoch, version] = split(revision), [priorEpoch, priorVersion] = split(this.revision ?? "");
    63	      if (epoch === priorEpoch ? Number(version) < Number(priorVersion) : this.revision !== undefined && order <= this.epochBarrier) return;
    64	      this.samples = [];
    65	      this.revision = revision;
    66	      // Every request already issued may still have reached the old process.
    67	      if (epoch !== priorEpoch) this.epochBarrier = this.order;
    68	    }
    69	    const before = this.offset, issuedBefore = this.issuedOffset;
    70	    const roundTrip = received - sent;
    71	    // Long responses use a conservative receipt date, never a midpoint that
    72	    // could latch half a server wait into the monotonic floor.
    73	    provisional ||= roundTrip > SHORT_RTT_MS;
    74	    this.samples = this.samples.filter(s => received >= s.received && received - s.received <= WINDOW_MS).slice(-(MAX_SAMPLES - 1));
    75	    this.samples.push({ offset: serverNow - (provisional ? received : (sent + received) / 2), roundTrip, received, provisional });
    76	    // Every short measured sample outranks provisional receipt stamps.
    77	    const best = this.samples.reduce((best, s) => s.provisional !== best.provisional ? (best.provisional ? s : best) : s.roundTrip <= best.roundTrip ? s : best);
    78	    this.offset = best.offset;
    79	    this.issuedOffset = best.offset;
    80	    if (before !== this.offset || issuedBefore !== this.issuedOffset) {
    81	      void this.persist().catch(() => {}); // Device calls/close await the same durable save.
    82	      // Watchers ignore sub-frame noise. A newly eligible issued offset can
    83	      // move even when a short sample merely confirms the server estimate.
    84	      const estimateShift = this.offset - before, issuedShift = (this.issuedOffset ?? 0) - (issuedBefore ?? 0);
    85	      const shift = Math.abs(issuedShift) > Math.abs(estimateShift) ? issuedShift : estimateShift;
   133	    // The server writes this stamp at the end of its hold, not at request send.
   134	    this.sample(serverNow, received, received, revision, order, true);
   135	  }
   136	  async attach(core: DeviceCore, deferPersistence = false) {
   137	    this.persistenceEnabled = !deferPersistence;
   138	    const kept = await core.call({ op: "meta", key: "server-clock" });
   139	    if (kept.denied) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(kept.denied));
   140	    try {
   141	      const state = JSON.parse(String(kept.ok)) as { offset: number; issuedOffset?: number } | null;
   142	      const issuedOffset = state?.issuedOffset ?? state?.offset;
   143	      if (state && Number.isFinite(state.offset) && Math.abs(state.offset) <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER && typeof issuedOffset === "number" && Number.isFinite(issuedOffset) && Math.abs(issuedOffset) <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) {
   144	        if (!this.samples.length) this.offset = state.offset;
   145	        this.issuedOffset ??= issuedOffset;
   146	      }
   147	    } catch { /* Missing or malformed clock metadata starts at offset zero. */ }
   148	    // Only admissions restore a durable floor. Old offset metadata's `last`
   149	    // may be a wall-time now() call and must not override a startup correction.
   150	    // The device commits this floor atomically with admission, and retains it
   151	    // after settlement. Pending entries also recover older stores/journals.
   152	    // Backfill legacy admission times transactionally before replay can retire
   153	    // the queue; offset persistence deliberately cannot retain an issued floor.
   154	    const pending = await core.call({ op: "queued", restore_clock_floor: true });
   155	    if (pending.denied) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(pending.denied));
   156	    const floor = await core.call({ op: "meta", key: "server-clock-floor" });
   157	    if (floor.denied) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(floor.denied));
   158	    const issued = Number(floor.ok);
   159	    if (Number.isSafeInteger(issued) && issued >= 0) this.last = Math.max(this.last, issued);
   160	    for (const entry of (pending.ok ?? []) as { now?: number }[]) {
   161	      if (Number.isSafeInteger(entry.now) && entry.now! >= 0) this.last = Math.max(this.last, entry.now!);
   162	    }
   163	    this.save = async value => {
   164	      const reply = await core.call({ op: "set_meta", key: "server-clock", value });
   165	      if (reply.denied) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(reply.denied));
   166	    };
   167	    await this.persist();
   168	  }

    57	/// The durable facts the authority kernel may read in one store transaction.
    58	/// Implementations perform access only; the policy below interprets records.
    59	pub(crate) trait AuthorityTransaction {
    60	    fn principal_generation(&self, principal: &str) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError>;
    61	    fn session_by_digest(&self, digest: &str) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    62	    fn latest_live_family_member(
    63	        &self,
    64	        principal: &str,
    65	        family: &str,
    66	        now: i64,
    67	    ) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    68	    fn work_by_id(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<WorkRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    69	    fn work_by_claimed_session_digest(
    70	        &self,
    71	        digest: &str,
    72	    ) -> Result<Option<WorkRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    73	
    74	    fn invalidate_session(&self, digest: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
    75	    fn invalidate_family(&self, principal: &str, family: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
    76	}

    78	pub(crate) enum AdmissionStanding {
    79	    SessionNotLive,
    80	    AuthorityNotLive,
    81	    Live(Authority),
    82	}
    83	
    84	/// Resolve the credential captured at admission. Refresh may replace its row,
    85	/// but the family and principal generation remain the durable authority.
    86	// @ref LLP 3000.009#5.1 — action authority is bound at admission and walked inside one transaction.
    87	pub(crate) fn admission_authority(
    88	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    89	    token_digest: &str,
    90	    principal: &str,
    91	    now: i64,
    92	) -> Result<AdmissionStanding, RuntimeError> {
    93	    let Some(session) = tx.session_by_digest(token_digest)? else {
    94	        return Ok(AdmissionStanding::SessionNotLive);
    95	    };
    96	    if !session.identity_is_valid() || session.scope != SessionScope::Full || session.principal != principal || session.expires_at <= now {
    97	        return Ok(AdmissionStanding::SessionNotLive);
    98	    }
    99	    let generation = tx.principal_generation(principal)?;
   100	    let Some(standing) = family_authority_expiry(tx, principal, &session.family, generation, now)?
   101	    else {
   102	        return Ok(AdmissionStanding::AuthorityNotLive);
   103	    };
   104	    Ok(AdmissionStanding::Live(Authority {
   105	        family: session.family,
   106	        generation,
   107	        expires_at: session.expires_at.min(standing),
   108	    }))
   109	}
   110	
   111	/// Walk a refresh/delegation family at one transaction snapshot. The admitted
   112	/// expiry is deliberately not an ongoing cap: refresh lifetime and admission
   113	/// lifetime are distinct. Claim leases and deadlines remain hard caps.
   114	pub(crate) fn family_authority_expiry(
   115	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
   116	    principal: &str,
   117	    family: &str,
   118	    generation: i64,
   119	    now: i64,
   120	) -> Result<Option<i64>, RuntimeError> {
   121	    if refuse_nul(&[(principal, "identity is not live"), (family, "identity is not live")]).is_err() { return Ok(None); }
   122	    let current_generation = tx.principal_generation(principal)?;
   123	    let (mut family, mut generation, mut bound) = (family.to_owned(), generation, i64::MAX);
   124	    let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
   125	    loop {
   126	        if refuse_nul(&[(&family, "identity is not live")]).is_err()
   127	            || generation != current_generation || !seen.insert(family.clone()) {
   128	            return Ok(None);
   129	        }
   130	        let Some(session) = tx.latest_live_family_member(principal, &family, now)? else {
   131	            return Ok(None);
   132	        };
   133	        if !session.identity_is_valid() || session.scope != SessionScope::Full { return Ok(None); }
   134	        bound = bound.min(session.expires_at);
   135	        if session.kind != "action" {
   136	            return Ok(Some(bound));
   137	        }
   138	        let Some(parent) = tx.work_by_claimed_session_digest(&session.digest)? else {
   139	            return Ok(None);
   140	        };
   141	        if parent.principal != principal || !claim_window_is_live(&parent, now) {
   142	            return Ok(None);
   143	        }
   144	        let lease = parent.lease_until.expect("a live claim has a lease");
   145	        bound = bound.min(lease).min(parent.deadline.unwrap_or(i64::MAX));
   146	        if let Some(service_generation) = parent.service_generation {
   147	            return Ok((service_generation == current_generation).then_some(bound));
   148	        }
   149	        match (parent.admission.family, parent.admission.generation) {
   150	            (Some(next), Some(next_generation)) => {
   151	                family = next;
   152	                generation = next_generation;
   153	            }
   154	            (None, None) => return Ok(Some(bound)), // Legacy work and development personas.
   155	            _ => return Ok(None),
   156	        }
   157	    }
   158	}
   159	
   160	pub(crate) fn work_authority_expiry(
   161	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
   162	    work: &WorkRecord,
   163	    now: i64,
   164	) -> Result<Option<i64>, RuntimeError> {
   165	    if refuse_nul(&[(&work.principal, "identity is not live"),
   166	        (work.admission.family.as_deref().unwrap_or(""), "identity is not live")]).is_err() { return Ok(None); }
   167	    if let Some(generation) = work.service_generation {
   168	        return Ok((tx.principal_generation(&work.principal)? == generation).then_some(i64::MAX));
   169	    }
   170	    match (&work.admission.family, work.admission.generation, work.admission.expires_at) {
   171	        (Some(family), Some(generation), Some(_)) => family_authority_expiry(
   172	            tx,
   173	            &work.principal,
   174	            family,
   175	            generation,
   176	            now,
   177	        ),
   178	        _ => Ok(Some(i64::MAX)), // Legacy rows and development personas.
   179	    }
   180	}
   181	
   182	fn claim_window_is_live(work: &WorkRecord, now: i64) -> bool {
   183	    work.state == "running"
   184	        && work.lease_until.is_some_and(|lease| lease > now)
   185	        && work.deadline.is_none_or(|deadline| deadline > now)
   186	}
   187	
   188	pub(crate) fn claim_is_owned(work: &WorkRecord, worker: &str, digest: &str) -> bool {
   189	    work.claimed_by.as_deref() == Some(worker) && work.session_digest.as_deref() == Some(digest)
   190	}
   191	
   192	pub(crate) fn live_claim_authority(
   193	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
   194	    digest: &str,
   195	    now: i64,
   196	) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   197	    let Some(work) = tx.work_by_claimed_session_digest(digest)? else {
   198	        return Ok(false);
   199	    };
   200	    Ok(claim_window_is_live(&work, now) && work_authority_expiry(tx, &work, now)?.is_some())
   201	}
   202	
   203	pub(crate) fn held_claim_authority(
   204	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
   205	    id: &str,
   206	    worker: &str,
   207	    digest: &str,
   208	    now: i64,
   209	) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   210	    let Some(work) = tx.work_by_id(id)? else {
   211	        return Ok(false);
   212	    };
   213	    if !claim_is_owned(&work, worker, digest) {
   214	        return Ok(false);
   215	    }
   216	    live_claim_authority(tx, digest, now)
   217	}
   218	
   219	pub(crate) fn live_session(
   220	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
   221	    digest: &str,
   222	    now: i64,
   223	) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError> {
   224	    let Some(session) = tx.session_by_digest(digest)? else {
   225	        return Ok(None);
   226	    };
   227	    if !session.identity_is_valid() || session.expires_at <= now {
   228	        return Ok(None);
   229	    }
   230	    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — revocation generations survive an older executable.
   231	    if session.scope == SessionScope::Read
   232	        && (session.cap_expires_at.is_none_or(|cap| cap <= now)
   233	            || session.principal_generation.is_none()
   234	            || session.principal_generation.unwrap() < tx.principal_generation(&session.principal)?) {
   235	        return Ok(None);
   236	    }
   237	    if session.kind == "action" && !live_claim_authority(tx, digest, now)? {
   238	        return Ok(None);
   239	    }
   240	    Ok(Some(session))
   241	}

   244	    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
   245	    digest: &str,

    49	/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
    50	pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    51	    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    52	    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    53	    let z = days + 719_468;
    54	    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    55	    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    56	    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    57	    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    58	    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    59	    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    60	    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    61	    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    62	    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
    63	}

    65	/// A positive duration in the units `clock advance` accepts, rounded up to a second.
    66	pub fn span(ms: i64) -> String {
    67	    let seconds = (ms.max(0) + 999) / 1_000;
    68	    let (d, h, m, s) = (seconds / 86_400, seconds % 86_400 / 3_600, seconds % 3_600 / 60, seconds % 60);
    69	    let parts: Vec<String> = [(d, "d"), (h, "h"), (m, "m"), (s, "s")].into_iter().filter(|(n, _)| *n > 0).map(|(n, unit)| format!("{n}{unit}")).collect();
    70	    if parts.is_empty() { "0s".into() } else { parts.join("") }
    71	}

    73	/// Each schedule's saved boundary, in declaration order.
    74	pub fn saved_boundaries(engine: &Engine) -> Vec<Option<i64>> {
    75	    engine.schema().schedules.iter()
    76	        .map(|schedule| {
    77	            let shape = engine.store().schedule_shape(&schedule.name).ok().flatten();
    78	            if shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|shape| *shape != snapback4_core::value::digest(schedule)) { return None; }
    79	            engine.store().schedule_boundary(&schedule.name).ok().flatten()
    80	        })
    81	        .collect()
    82	}

    84	/// Preflight is bounded before the clock or worker leases change.
    85	// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — only explicit execution enumerates all crossed windows; coalesced reports keep a bounded preview.
    86	pub fn crossed_boundaries(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool) -> Result<Vec<(usize, i64)>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    87	    let mut boundaries = Vec::new();
    88	    let mut report_bytes = 0usize;
    89	    for (index, schedule) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate() {
    90	        // JSON may escape every error byte; count that bound per schedule.
    91	        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add(2048 + 6 * (REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3) + 8 * (schedule.name.len() + schedule.target.len()));
    92	        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule report exceeds its byte budget; reduce the declared schedules")); }
    93	        if held { continue; }
    94	        let Some(old) = before.get(index).copied().flatten() else { continue; };
    95	        let end = schedule.boundary(now);
    96	        if old >= end { continue; }
    97	        let periods = schedule.periods_between(old, end);
    98	        if each_boundary && periods > (10_000 - boundaries.len()) as i64 {
    99	            return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("--each-boundary crosses more than 10000 schedule windows; use a smaller duration or omit --each-boundary to coalesce"));
   100	        }
   101	        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add((if each_boundary { periods as usize } else { (periods as usize).min(SKIPPED_PREVIEW + 1) }).saturating_mul(1024 + 8 * schedule.target.len()));
   102	        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule window report exceeds its byte budget; use a smaller duration")); }
   103	        if !each_boundary { continue; }
   104	        let mut boundary = schedule.next(old);
   105	        while boundary <= end {
   106	            boundaries.push((index, boundary));
   107	            boundary = schedule.next(boundary);
   108	        }
   109	    }
   110	    boundaries.sort_by_key(|(index, at)| (*at, *index));
   111	    Ok(boundaries)
   112	}

   114	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — no silent successful advance behind retained schedule markers.
   115	pub fn refuse_held(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64) -> Result<(), snapback4_core::Refusal> {
   116	    for (schedule, saved) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(before) {
   117	        if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| *saved >= schedule.boundary(now) && *saved > schedule.boundary(snapback4_core::now_ms())) {
   118	            let due = schedule.next(saved);
   119	            return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_HELD", "clock", format!(
   120	                "schedule {} already processed boundary {}; requested clock {} has not reached its next window {}. Nothing advanced. Advance {} or use a fresh staging deployment; allowHeld:true explicitly accepts this hold. Never rewind saved boundaries",
   121	                schedule.name, utc(saved), utc(now), utc(due), format!("{}ms", due - now))).guide("clock"));
   122	        }
   123	    }
   124	    Ok(())
   125	}

   131	/// What each schedule did on one clock advance, and why one did not fire.
   132	/// The core fires each schedule at most once per advance, for the latest
   133	/// boundary, and holds it while its saved boundary is ahead of the clock.
   134	// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — missed boundaries fire once; this only explains them.
   135	pub fn schedule_report(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], fired: &[String], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool, port: Option<u16>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
   136	    let after = saved_boundaries(engine);
   137	    // Read only bounded summaries: job args/cursors and full error payloads
   138	    // are irrelevant to this report and must not be loaded then replicated.
   139	    let runs = job_summaries(engine).unwrap_or_default();
   140	    engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| {
   141	        let (old, saved) = (before.get(index).copied().flatten(), after.get(index).copied().flatten());
   142	        let current = schedule.boundary(now);
   143	        let next = schedule.next(current);
   144	        let mut entry = serde_json::json!({ "name": schedule.name, "target": schedule.target, "period": period(schedule), "fired": false, "firedWindows": [], "skippedBoundaries": [], "nextBoundary": utc(next) });
   145	        if fired.contains(&schedule.name) {
   146	            let end = saved.unwrap_or(current);
   147	            entry["fired"] = true.into();
   148	            let start = schedule.previous(end);
   149	            let window = |boundary| serde_json::json!({"periodStart": schedule.previous(boundary), "periodEnd": boundary});
   150	            let mut windows = Vec::new();
   155	                }
   156	            } else { windows.push(window(end)); }
   157	            if each_boundary {
   158	                entry["reason"] = format!("fired {} windows: {}", windows.len(), windows.iter().map(|window| format!("{} to {}", utc(window["periodStart"].as_i64().unwrap()), utc(window["periodEnd"].as_i64().unwrap()))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ")).into();
   159	            }
   160	            entry["firedWindows"] = windows.into();
   161	            entry["periodStart"] = start.into();
   162	            entry["periodEnd"] = end.into();
   163	            if !each_boundary { entry["reason"] = format!("fired for the period {} to {}", utc(start), utc(end)).into(); }
   164	            if let Some(run) = runs.get(&schedule.target) { entry["run"] = run.clone(); }
   165	            // @ref LLP 3000.040#24-monthly-and-yearly-schedules — calendar periods count boundaries, not milliseconds.
   166	            let skipped = if each_boundary { 0 } else { old.map(|old| schedule.periods_between(old, end) - 1).unwrap_or(0) };
   167	            if skipped > 0 {
   168	                entry["skippedPeriods"] = skipped.into();
   169	                let mut windows = Vec::new();
   170	                let mut at = schedule.next(old.unwrap());
   171	                while at < end && windows.len() < SKIPPED_PREVIEW {
   172	                    let mut item = window(at);
   173	                    let mut args = serde_json::Map::new();
   174	                    if let Some(program) = engine.program(&schedule.target) {
   175	                        if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") { args.insert("periodStart".into(), schedule.previous(at).into()); }
   176	                        if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") { args.insert("periodEnd".into(), at.into()); }
   177	                    }
   178	                    item["command"] = format!("snapback4 run {} '{}'{}", schedule.target, serde_json::Value::Object(args), port.map(|port| format!(" --port {port}")).unwrap_or_default()).into();
   179	                    windows.push(item); at = schedule.next(at);
   180	                }
   181	                entry["skippedBoundariesOmitted"] = (skipped - windows.len() as i64).into();
   182	                entry["skippedBoundaries"] = windows.into();
   183	                entry["reason"] = format!("fired once, for the latest period {} to {}; {skipped} earlier period{} this advance crossed (from {}) did not run: missed boundaries fire once. Run {} with periodStart/periodEnd for an earlier period",
   184	                    utc(start), utc(end), if skipped == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, utc(old.unwrap_or(end)), schedule.target).into();
   185	            }
   186	        } else if held {
   187	            entry["holdCode"] = "disabled".into();
   188	            entry["reason"] = "schedules are held (dev --hold-schedules or --replay); a restart without the flag resumes at the next boundary".into();
   189	        } else if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| old.is_some() && (*saved > current || *saved == current && *saved > schedule.boundary(snapback4_core::now_ms()))) {
   190	            let due = schedule.next(saved);
   191	            entry["holdCode"] = "saved-boundary".into();
   192	            entry["savedBoundary"] = saved.into();
   193	            entry["heldUntil"] = utc(due).into();
   194	            entry["nextBoundary"] = utc(due).into();
   195	            entry["reason"] = format!("held by the store: boundary {} was already processed and this clock {} has not reached its next window (restarting resets the process offset, not the saved boundary).    196	                utc(saved), utc(now), span(due - now)).into();
   197	        } else if old != saved {
   198	            entry["holdCode"] = "initialized".into();
   199	            entry["reason"] = format!("{} started at boundary {}: a schedule fires at the boundary after the first one it sees, next {} ({} from now)",
   200	                if old.is_none() { "this schedule" } else { "this changed schedule" }, utc(saved.unwrap_or(current)), utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
   201	        } else {
   202	            entry["holdCode"] = "not-due".into();
   203	            entry["reason"] = format!("next boundary {} ({} from now; schedule times are UTC)", utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
   204	        }
   205	        entry
   206	    }).collect()
   207	}

     3	 * The transport still consumes its response; its owner fences any adoption. */
     4	export function waitForCaller<T>(work: Promise<T>, stopped: AbortSignal, known = () => false): Promise<T | undefined> {
     5	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
     6	    const clean = () => stopped.removeEventListener("abort", stop);
     7	    const stop = () => { clean(); if (!known()) resolve(undefined); };
     8	    stopped.addEventListener("abort", stop, { once: true });
     9	    if (stopped.aborted) stop();
    10	    void work.then(value => { clean(); resolve(value); }, error => { clean(); reject(error); });
    11	  });
    12	}

    19	import { StorageWarning } from "./app-storage.ts";
    20	import { OnlineCapture, markedId, type CaptureRecord } from "./online-capture.ts";
    21	
    22	/** Private implementation; the returned client has the unchanged Client card. */
    23	export async function onlineCustody(raw: Client, url: string, store: SessionStore, report: (error: unknown) => void, autoStart = true,
    24	  captureAuthority?: AdmissionAuthorityContext) {
    25	  const viewer = raw.viewer()!;
    26	  const key = storeKey("writes", url, viewer);
    27	  // @ref LLP 3000.013.000#4 — a device-less browser app captures each click
    28	  // synchronously; once committed, the journal below owns it as before.
    29	  const capture = captureAuthority ? new OnlineCapture(url, viewer, captureAuthority) : undefined;
    30	  // @ref LLP 3000.013.000#4.4 — captured admissions wait behind recovery, from before signed-in.
    31	  let recovery: Promise<void> | undefined, openGate: (() => void) | undefined;
    32	  if (capture) recovery = new Promise<void>(resolve => { openGate = resolve; });
    33	  // Ids durable in the journal that this runtime replays without capturing; settled ids leave.
    34	  const restoredIds = new Set<string>();
    35	  let active = true;
    36	  let storeRefusal: Refusal | undefined;
    37	  let retirement: Promise<void> | undefined;
    38	  const ids = new MutationIds();
    39	  const emissions = new WriteHistory();
    40	  // I13: failed receipt persistence cannot turn a known outcome back into
    41	  // pending, even after the raw client's bounded history evicts that id.
    42	  const unpersisted = new Map<string, Terminal>();
    43	  // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.3 — failed status saves cannot hide this runtime's
    44	  // observed hold. This overlays presentation only; the journal still owns FIFO.
    45	  const unsavedHolds = new Map<string, { reason: string; revision: string | undefined }>();
    46	  const dispatchRevisions = new Map<string, string | undefined>();
    47	  const recoveredIntents = new Set<string>();
    48	  const listeners = new Set<(write: Terminal) => void>();
    49	  const pending = pendingChanges();
    50	  const identification = new IdentityWait(pending.notify);
    51	  const rawIntents = pendingIntentAccess(raw);
    52	  const intentScope = () => active && !storeRefusal && raw.viewer() === viewer ? rawIntents.scope() : undefined;
    53	  const presentation = new OnlineIntentPresentation(intentScope, pending.notify);
    54	  const stopPending = raw.onPendingWrites?.(pending.notify);
    55	  let writes: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
    56	  const read = journalReader(key, viewer, url, store, report);
    57	  const change = <T>(work: (journal: Journal) => T, recoverExisting = false): Promise<T> => {
    58	    const result = locked(key, async () => {
    59	      const journal = await read(true);
    60	      const before = recoverExisting ? JSON.stringify(journal) : undefined;
    61	      const value = work(journal);
    62	      capture?.collect(journal);
    63	      const after = JSON.stringify(journal);
    64	      // Reading an existing intent/receipt needs no new custody. A redundant
    65	      // save must not turn that known outcome into an admission refusal.
    66	      if (after !== before) { await store.set(key, after); journalEvents.notify(); }
    67	      return value;
    68	    });
    69	    writes = result;
    70	    return result;
    71	  };
    72	  // @ref LLP 3000.013.000#4.2 — journal lock, then session lock, raw store only:
    73	  // the click's session must still hold when its intent and marker commit.
    74	  const sessionEnded = Symbol("session ended");
    75	  // One normalized comparison (MutationIds' input key) for admission and recovery.
    76	  const sameInput = (a: { op: string; args: unknown }, b: { op: string; args: unknown }) => {
    77	    try { return inputKey(a.op, a.args) === inputKey(b.op, b.args); } catch { return false; }
    78	  };
    79	  const admitCaptured = <T>(record: CaptureRecord, work: (journal: Journal) => T): Promise<{ value: Awaited<T>; known: boolean } | typeof sessionEnded> => {
    80	    const result = locked(key, () => locked(record.authority.key, async () => {
    81	      if (!await capture!.holds(record)) return sessionEnded;
    82	      const journal = await read(true);
    83	      const before = JSON.stringify(journal);
    84	      const value = await work(journal);
    85	      // A refusal of an unknown id (input reuse, saturation) keeps no marker.
    86	      const known = journal.pending.some(intent => intent.id === record.id && sameInput(intent, record))
    87	        || (value as Write | undefined)?.state === "sent"
    88	        || ((value as Write | undefined)?.state === "failed" && !["E_WRITE_ID_REUSE"].includes((value as Extract<Write, { state: "failed" }>).why.code)
    89	          && (journal.receipts.some(write => write.id === record.id) || !!journal.retired?.includes(record.id) || markedId(journal, record.id)));
    90	      if (known) capture!.mark(journal, record);
    91	      capture!.collect(journal);
    92	      const after = JSON.stringify(journal);
    93	      if (after !== before) { await store.set(key, after); journalEvents.notify(); }
    94	      return { value, known };
    95	    }));
    96	    writes = result;
    97	    return result;
    98	  };
    99	  let recoveryDelay = 1_000, recoveryTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
   100	  const scheduleRecovery = () => {
   101	    if (!capture || recoveryTimer || !active) return;
   102	    recoveryTimer = setTimeout(() => { recoveryTimer = undefined; if (capture.stale && active) void recover(); }, recoveryDelay);
   103	    (recoveryTimer as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
   104	    recoveryDelay = Math.min(recoveryDelay * 2, 60_000);
   105	  };
   106	  const terminal = (write: Write): write is Terminal => write.state !== "pending"
   107	    && !(write.state === "failed" && ["E_CLOSED", "E_AUTH"].includes(write.why.code));
   108	  const notify = (write: Terminal) => {
   109	    unsavedHolds.delete(write.id);
   110	    dispatchRevisions.delete(write.id);
   111	    restoredIds.delete(write.id);
   112	    ids.finish(write.id);
   113	    pending.notify();
   114	    if (active && emissions.firstEmission(write.id)) for (const listener of listeners) listener(write);
   115	  };
   116	  // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — recovery confirms execution, never historical result values or details.
   117	  const receiptOf = (write: Terminal): Terminal => write.state === "sent"
   118	    ? { state: "sent", id: write.id, seq: write.seq, replayed: true }
   119	    : { state: "failed", id: write.id, why: { code: write.why.code, family: write.why.family, message: ["E_STORE_REPLACED", "E_DEV_RESET", "E_STORE_RESTORE"].includes(write.why.code) ? `write refused: ${write.why.code}; whether it executed is unknown; do not retry automatically` : `write refused: ${write.why.code}` } };
   120	  const retain = (write: Terminal, error: unknown) => {
   121	    const first = !unpersisted.has(write.id);
   122	    if (active) unpersisted.set(write.id, receiptOf(write));
   123	    if (first) notify(write);
   124	    report(error);
   125	  };
   126	  const journalEntries = (journal: Journal) => journal.pending.map(intent => {
   127	    const hold = unsavedHolds.get(intent.id);
   128	    const reason = (hold?.revision === intent.statusRevision ? hold?.reason : undefined) ?? intent.holdReason;
   129	    return { id: intent.id, op: intent.op, args: intent.args, predicted: [],
   130	      ...(reason ? { state: "held" as const, reason } : { state: intent.dispatched ? "sent" as const : "queued" as const }) };
   131	  });
   132	  const settle = async (write: Terminal) => {
   133	    await change(journal => {
   134	      const intent = journal.pending.find(intent => intent.id === write.id);
   135	      if (!intent) return false;
   136	      presentation.sync(journalEntries(journal), journal.receipts);
   137	      presentation.settled(write, { id: intent.id, op: intent.op, args: intent.args, predicted: [], state: intent.dispatched ? "sent" : "queued" });
   138	      journal.pending = journal.pending.filter(intent => intent.id !== write.id);
   139	      // Never persist historical read results or refusal details for disclosure on reopen.
   140	      journal.receipts.push(receiptOf(write));
   141	      keepReceipts(journal, new Set([write.id]), write.state === "failed" && ["E_STORE_REPLACED", "E_DEV_RESET", "E_STORE_RESTORE"].includes(write.why.code));
   142	      return true;
   143	    });
   144	    presentation.release(write.id);
   145	    // Durable retirement belongs to the shared journal; notification and

   192	 * the callback; it carries only that arm's token, never another handler's writes.
   193	 */
   194	export async function witnessForm<T>(app: App, event: Event | { nativeEvent: Event }, handler: (mutate: App["mutate"]) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
   195	  const native = "nativeEvent" in event ? event.nativeEvent : event;

   197	    claimHandler(owner: App, event: Event): { mutate: App["mutate"]; done(): void } | undefined;
   198	  } }).__snapback4Witness;
   199	  const claim = bridge?.claimHandler(app, native);
   200	  try { return await handler(claim?.mutate ?? app.mutate.bind(app)); }
   201	  finally { claim?.done(); }

    57	        else if (!response.ok || json.ok !== true || !["full", "read"].includes(String(json.scope)) || typeof json.store_id !== "string") why = readOnlyRefusal("E_READ_ONLY_UNSUPPORTED");
    58	        else if (json.scope !== "read") why = readOnlyRefusal("E_READ_ONLY_CREDENTIAL");
    59	        else { this.accept(json); this.accepted = this.key(); }
    60	      } catch (error) { why = transportRefusal(error); }
    61	      if (why && key === this.key() && !why.retryable) this.failed = { key, why };
    62	      return why;
    63	    })();
    64	    this.pending = { key, work };
    65	    void work.finally(() => { if (this.pending?.work === work) this.pending = undefined; });
    66	    return work;
    67	  }
    68	}

   474	  function observeStore(json: Record<string, unknown>, floorAtDispatch: number, receipt = false, touched?: Changes): void {
   475	    if (storeRefusal) return;
   476	    const why = (json.denied ?? json.why) as Refusal | undefined;
   477	    if (why?.code === "E_STORE_REPLACED" || why?.code === "E_DEV_RESET" || why?.code === "E_STORE_RESTORE") { stopForStore(why.code); return; }

   479	    if (typeof id !== "string" || !id) return; // Older servers have no identity envelope.
   480	    if (storeIdentity !== undefined && id !== storeIdentity) { stopForStore("E_STORE_REPLACED"); return; }
   481	    storeIdentity = id;
   482	    if (typeof json.generation === "number" && Number.isSafeInteger(json.generation) && json.generation > queryGeneration) {
   483	      queryGeneration = json.generation; pendingEvents.notify();
   484	    }
   485	    if (dispatch.store !== id) { dispatch.store = id; dispatch.owner?.observe(id); }
   486	    // Replayed receipts name a historical commit; their head is the current
   487	    // store watermark. A buffered response may predate a later observed write,
   488	    // so restoration compares with the floor at dispatch, not at delivery.
   489	    const head = receipt && json.replayed === true ? json.head : json.head ?? json.seq;
   490	    if (typeof head !== "number" || !Number.isSafeInteger(head) || head < 0) return;
   491	    if (head < floorAtDispatch) { stopForStore("E_STORE_RESTORE"); return; }
   492	    if (head > minimumReadSeq) queryChanges.change(head, touched);
   493	    minimumReadSeq = Math.max(minimumReadSeq, head);

    14	// Charge consumed CPU for pacing, not time the OS already kept this thread off
    15	// CPU. The cooperative chunk deadline still uses wall time. A failed clock
    16	// sample falls back to the more conservative wall-time pause.
    17	struct SliceClock { wall: Instant, cpu: Option<Duration> }
    18	impl SliceClock {
    19	    fn start() -> Self { Self { wall: Instant::now(), cpu: Self::cpu_time() } }
    20	    fn cpu_time() -> Option<Duration> {
    21	        let mut at = libc::timespec { tv_sec: 0, tv_nsec: 0 };
    22	        if unsafe { libc::clock_gettime(libc::CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, &mut at) } != 0 { return None; }
    23	        Some(Duration::new(at.tv_sec.try_into().ok()?, at.tv_nsec.try_into().ok()?))
    24	    }
    25	    fn consumed(&self) -> Duration {
    26	        self.cpu.zip(Self::cpu_time()).and_then(|(start, end)| end.checked_sub(start)).unwrap_or_else(|| self.wall.elapsed())
    27	    }
    28	}

    30	// Detached readers do not take engine tickets. Sample OS load as well as the
    31	// round-3 engine contention signal; cache the syscall for 100 ms. Load includes
    32	// other tenants and trails short bursts, so this is a pacing hint, not admission.
    33	fn host_contended() -> bool {
    34	    use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};
    35	    static SAMPLE: Mutex<(Option<Instant>, bool)> = Mutex::new((None, false));
    36	    static CPUS: OnceLock<usize> = OnceLock::new();
    37	    let mut sample = lock(&SAMPLE);
    38	    if sample.0.is_none_or(|at| at.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(100)) {
    39	        let mut load = 0.0;
    40	        let cpus = *CPUS.get_or_init(|| std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get()));
    41	        sample.1 = unsafe { libc::getloadavg(&mut load, 1) } == 1 && load >= cpus as f64;
    42	        sample.0 = Some(Instant::now());
    43	    }
    44	    sample.1
    45	}

    47	fn engine_work<T>(shared: &Shared, run: impl FnOnce(&mut snapback4_core::Engine, Duration) -> T) -> T {
    48	    let mut engine = shared.engine.background();

    53	    // notification and mistake maintenance for a newly arrived request.

    70	fn work_at(shared: &Shared, drain: bool, tick: u64, schedule_sample: Option<i64>) -> Result<Work, RuntimeError> {
    71	    let mut work = Work::default();
    72	    shared.ephemeral.sweep(shared.now())?;
    73	    work.delivery_chunks = delivery(shared, drain)?;
    74	    loop {
    75	        if phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.run_view_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget)), drain, "view recount")?.is_none() {break;}
    76	        work.chunks += 1;
    77	        if !drain && work.chunks >= 500 {break;}
    78	        std::thread::yield_now();
    79	    }
    80	    loop {
    81	        let swept = phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.sweep_expired_for(shared.now(), 2_000, budget)), drain, "the expiry sweep")?;
    82	        work.expired += swept;
    83	        if !drain || swept == 0 { break; }
    84	    }
    85	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.2 — advancing a replay clock does not release its schedule hold.
    86	    if !shared.hold_schedules {
    87	        let fired = phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, _| {
    88	            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.2 — select advance windows before draining; admission deadlines still use the live advanced clock.
    89	            if let Some(sample) = schedule_sample {
    90	                let windows = engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| (index, schedule.boundary(sample))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    91	                let mut fired = Vec::new();
    92	                for (index, boundary) in windows { fired.extend(engine.fire_schedule_boundary_at(shared.now(), index, boundary)?); }
    93	                Ok(fired)
    94	            } else { engine.fire_schedules(shared.now()) }
    95	        }), drain, "schedules")?;
    96	        work.schedules = fired.len();
    97	        for name in &fired { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: schedule {name} fired"); }
    98	        work.fired = fired;
    99	    }
   100	    while drain || work.chunks < 500 {
   101	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { break; }
   102	        let (run, logs) = engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| {
   103	            let run = engine.run_job_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget);
   104	            (run, engine.take_native_logs())
   105	        });
   106	        for line in logs { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: native {line}"); }
   107	        let Some(run) = phase(shared, run, drain, "job")? else { break; };
   108	        work.chunks += 1;
   109	        match run.state {
   110	            snapback4_core::JobState::Done => snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} done: {} chunk{}, {} row{} written", run.name, run.chunks, if run.chunks == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, run.rows_written, if run.rows_written == 1 { "" } else { "s" }),
   111	            snapback4_core::JobState::Parked => {
   112	                work.parked += 1;
   113	                if shared.personas { shared.refusals.job(&run); }
   114	                snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} parked after {} chunks: {}", run.name, run.chunks, run.error.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
   115	            }
   116	            _ => {}
   117	        }
   118	        // FIFO engine admission hands waiting requests their turn before the
   119	        // next chunk; yield_now alone cannot make that promise for a mutex.
   120	    }
   121	    if drain || tick % 5 == 0 {
   122	        loop {
   123	            let actions = phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.requeue_expired_actions_for(shared.now(), budget)), drain, "the action lease sweep")?;
   124	            let effects = phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.requeue_expired_effects_for(shared.now(), budget)), drain, "the effect lease sweep")?;
   125	            if actions + effects > 0 { shared.durable_committed(&lock(&shared.engine)); }
   126	            if effects > 0 { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: {effects} effect lease{} expired; queued again", if effects == 1 { "" } else { "s" }); }
   127	            if !drain || actions + effects == 0 { break; }
   128	        }
   129	    }
   130	    if drain || tick % 60 == 0 {
   131	        phase(shared, (|| {
   132	            let mut sweep = engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.prepare_asset_sweep_for(shared.now(), budget))?;
   133	            sweep.remove_files()?;
   134	            while !sweep.is_empty() { engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.finish_asset_sweep_for(&mut sweep, budget))?; }
   135	            Ok(())
   136	        })(), drain, "the asset sweep")?;
   137	    }
   138	    Ok(work)
   139	}

   141	fn delivery(shared: &Shared, drain: bool) -> Result<usize, RuntimeError> {
   142	    let mut chunks = 0;
   143	    while drain || chunks < 500 {
   144	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { break; }
   145	        if phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.run_timeline_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget)), drain, "timeline delivery")?.is_none() { break; }
   146	        chunks += 1;
   147	    }
   148	    Ok(chunks)
   149	}

   253	fn timely(shared: &Shared, tick: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   254	    phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.sweep_expired_for(shared.now(), 2_000, budget)), false, "the expiry sweep")?;
   255	    if !shared.hold_schedules {
   256	        let count = timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, _| Ok(engine.schema().schedules.len()))?;
   257	        for index in 0..count {
   258	            // One atomic boundary per admission, never the entire schedule set.
   259	            // Adoption between slices is harmless: the next tick visits its set.
   260	            let fired = phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, _| engine.fire_schedule_at(shared.now(), index)), false, "schedules")?;
   261	            for name in fired { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: schedule {name} fired"); }
   262	        }
   263	    }
   264	    if tick % 5 == 0 {
   265	        phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| {
   266	            let result = engine.requeue_expired_actions_for(shared.now(), budget);
   267	            if result.as_ref().is_ok_and(|n| *n > 0) { shared.durable_committed(engine); }
   268	            result
   269	        }), false, "the action lease sweep")?;
   270	        let effects = phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| {
   271	            let result = engine.requeue_expired_effects_for(shared.now(), budget);
   272	            if result.as_ref().is_ok_and(|n| *n > 0) { shared.durable_committed(engine); }
   273	            result
   274	        }), false, "the effect lease sweep")?;
   275	        if effects > 0 { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: {effects} effect leases expired; queued again"); }
   276	    }
   277	    if tick % 60 == 0 {
   278	        phase(shared, (|| {
   279	            let Some(mut sweep) = timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.prepare_asset_sweep_for(shared.now(), budget).map(Some))? else { return Ok(()); };
   280	            // Bounded stale batch; filesystem work owns no engine lock.
   281	            sweep.remove_files()?;
   282	            while !sweep.is_empty() {
   283	                // A clock drain that began between file removal and retirement
   284	                // owns the sweep now. Its durable metadata also permits retry
   285	                // on the next asset tick; do not spin on skipped slices.
   286	                if timely_engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.finish_asset_sweep_for(&mut sweep, budget))? == 0 { break; }
   287	            }
   288	            Ok(())
   289	        })(), false, "the asset sweep")?;
   290	    }
   291	    Ok(())
   292	}

   294	pub(super) fn maintain(shared: Arc<Shared>) {
   295	    let mut tick = 0;
   296	    let mut last_tick = Instant::now();
   297	    loop {
   298	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
   299	        {
   300	            let state = lock(&shared.maintenance);
   301	            if !state.advancing && !state.paused && let Err(error) = shared.ephemeral.sweep(shared.now()) { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: ephemeral sweep: {error}"); }
   302	        }
   303	        if last_tick.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
   304	            tick += 1; last_tick = Instant::now();
   305	            // One bounded reclamation slice; abandoned bytes remain charged
   306	            // until their actual records are dropped. No engine lock is held.
   307	            lock(&shared.following).reclaim(shared.now(), snapback4_core::Ceilings { heap_bytes: 1 << 20, ..Default::default() });
   308	            if let Err(error) = timely(&shared, tick) { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: maintenance failed: {error}"); }
   309	        }
   310	        promote_aged(&shared, Instant::now());
   311	        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
   312	    }
   313	}
   314	
   315	fn promote_aged(shared: &Shared, now: Instant) {
   316	    if lock(&shared.maintenance).eligible(now, true) { bulk_slice(shared, true); }
   317	}
   318	
   319	pub(super) fn bulk(shared: Arc<Shared>) {
   320	    loop {
   321	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
   322	        let observed = *lock(&shared.seq);
   323	        let mut did_work = false;
   324	        for _ in 0..3 {
   325	            if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
   326	            did_work |= bulk_slice(&shared, false);
   327	            let pause = lock(&shared.maintenance).resume_at.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
   328	            if !pause.is_zero() {
   329	                // No shared lock survives this pause. Request commits do not
   330	                // cancel repayment; empty kinds do not idle an active cycle.
   331	                std::thread::sleep(pause.min(Duration::from_millis(100)));
   332	            }
   333	        }
   334	        if !did_work {
   335	            loop {
   336	                let pause = lock(&shared.maintenance).empty_cycle(Instant::now());
   337	                if pause.is_zero() { break; }
   338	                std::thread::sleep(pause.min(Duration::from_millis(100)));
   339	            }
   340	            let seq = lock(&shared.seq);
   341	            if *seq == observed {
   342	                drop(shared.committed.wait_timeout(seq, Duration::from_millis(100)).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()));
   343	            }
   344	        }
   345	    }
   346	}

+## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)
+
+Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
+Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
+LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
+and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
+intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
+This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.
+
+### Session input and compatibility
+
+Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
+principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
+Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
+transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
+expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
+server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
+as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
+and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
+E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
+one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
+shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
+the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.
+
+### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries
+
+ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
+for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
+coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.
+
+For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
+lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
+fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
+in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
+the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
+become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
+refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
+families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
+Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
+deadlines/backoffs remain business time.
+
+Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
+response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
+and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
+through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
+new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
+such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
+including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
+time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
+bearer's matching request URL/header, monotonically increases expiry/cap and
+persists through existing credential/custody fences before clock listeners run.
+Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
+evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
+clock publication are serialized: durable local credential saves are awaited
+before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
+clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
+transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
+App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
+clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
+App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
+the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
+and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
+The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
+spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
+reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
+local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
+auth operation or remote revocation queue.
+Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
+before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
+An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
+completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
+Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
+clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
+own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
+an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
+staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
+without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
+reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
+check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
+absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
+and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
+ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
+credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
+business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
+all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
+credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
+This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
+ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.
+
+advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
+before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
+queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
+so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
+row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
+host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
+same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
+and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
+The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
+clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
+automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
+report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
+drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
+work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.
+
+A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
+E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
+schedule, saved boundary, next window and recovery duration. Fresh staging
+storage and continuing with the original offset are recovery choices; saved
+markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
+retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
+explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
+Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.
+
+### Upgrade advice and future formats
+
+Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
+version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
+for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
+The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
+older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
+that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
+Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
+guide changes remains available. No ancestor
+process inspection or script mutation is introduced.
+
+The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
+uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
+nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
+never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
+Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
+Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
+nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.
+
+### Starter and proof rendering
+
+Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and
+partial empty results retain distinct text, with existing freshness and
+pagination semantics unchanged. Rename the docs' local ReadState example to
+ReadNotice so it does not shadow the export. Password clients omit persona
+selection and explicit web witness/generated API imports. The proof driver installs the
+existing witness bridge before app creation; createApp calls an immutable Symbol observer only under explicit witness=web.
+This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication
+boundary. A witness URL alone installs no observer and exposes no App global.
+The driver installs its nonconfigurable/nonwritable observer before application
+scripts and locks/freezes the selected witness bridge; the first App remains
+selected for that page. Same-App explicit API registration can enrich it;
+a different explicit App refuses E_WITNESS_APP_SELECTION and requires a separate
+page. Later automatic Apps cannot silently redirect the proof. Application JS
+remains trusted to implement the application: same-origin code can forge its
+own test observer outside a driven page, just as it can read web session storage.
+The observer grants no new credentials or backend authority. Ordinary bundles
+carry only the creation dispatch, not the witness implementation. No-API
+registration captures only durable non-ephemeral mutation handles; direct
+witness mutate still requires generated API.
+
+Proof text locators match normalized entire descendant text, including composed
+React Native spans and wrapping labels. Choose smallest matching visible,
+non-editable elements; independent matches retain strict Playwright ambiguity.
+Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,
+with no Unicode normalization or input value matching. Exact strings are case-sensitive;
+explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
+String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
+fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
+Text ranges outside overflow clips do not contribute evidence to a visible
+ancestor. Layoutless wrappers may forward their visible descendants; a clipped
+suffix cannot manufacture a complete status label.
+

    76	      if (element && (/^(INPUT|TEXTAREA|SCRIPT|STYLE|NOSCRIPT|TEMPLATE)$/.test(element.tagName) || element.isContentEditable)) return { text: "", matched: false };
    77	      const style = element ? getComputedStyle(element) : null;
    78	      if (style?.display === "none" || style?.opacity === "0") return { text: "", matched: false };
    79	      const suppressed = style ? style.visibility === "hidden" || style.visibility === "collapse" : ancestorSuppressed;
    80	      const nodes = element?.shadowRoot ? element.shadowRoot.childNodes
    81	        : element?.tagName === "SLOT" ? ((element as HTMLSlotElement).assignedNodes({flatten:true}).length ? (element as HTMLSlotElement).assignedNodes({flatten:true}) : element.childNodes) : node.childNodes;
    82	      let text = "", descendantMatch = false;
    83	      for (const child of nodes) {
    84	        const result = walk(child, suppressed);
    85	        // Block boundaries are whitespace, never concatenated words from
    86	        // unrelated paragraph siblings. Inline RN spans retain their text.
    87	        const block = child.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE && /^(block|flex|grid|table|list-item)/.test(getComputedStyle(child as Element).display);
    88	        text += block ? ` ${result.text} ` : result.text;
    89	        descendantMatch ||= result.matched;
    90	      }
    91	      const normalized = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    92	      const box = element?.getBoundingClientRect();
    93	      const visible = element && !suppressed && box && box.width > 0 && box.height > 0;
    94	      const ownMatch = !!visible && !/^(HTML|BODY)$/.test(element.tagName) && matches(normalized);
    95	      if (ownMatch && !descendantMatch) found.push(element);
    96	      return { text, matched: ownMatch || descendantMatch };
    97	    };
    98	    observedText = walk(root).text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    99	    return found;
   100	  }
   101	  return { queryAll, query: (root: Document | Element | ShadowRoot, selector: string) => queryAll(root, selector)[0] ?? null,
   102	    text: (root: Element) => { queryAll(root, '{"source":"","flags":"","regex":false,"exact":true}'); return observedText; } };
   103	}
   104	
   105	export function visibleText(locator: Locator, timeout: number): Promise<string> {
   106	  // Build the function in Node, then let Playwright serialize it. Passing an
   107	  // arrow as a string would evaluate to the function rather than invoke it.
   108	  const reader = new Function("element", `return (${renderedTextEngine.toString()})().text(element);`) as (element: Element) => string;
   109	  return locator.evaluate(reader, undefined, { timeout });
   110	}
   111

   113	// Await registration before exposing the synchronous locator constructor.
   114	try { await registerRenderedSelector((await import("playwright-core")).selectors); }
   115	catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND" && (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "MODULE_NOT_FOUND") throw error; }

- **[P2] Ordinary current schedule windows can block maintenance recovery.** At frozen `snapback4/crates/snapback4/src/dev_clock_store.rs:117`, `refuse_held` compares saved boundaries with wall time. With an hourly schedule, `advance("2h")`, then `advance("1ms", {drain:false})`, then `drain()` rejects with `E_CLOCK_HELD`: the saved boundary equals the current simulated window and exceeds wall time. No restart or future boundary is required. Maintenance remains paused unless callers add `allowHeld:true`. The same condition can obstruct recovery after a drain fails after enqueueing its current boundary. This conflicts with §11’s successful not-due behavior and zero-time drain recovery; the preflight is invoked at frozen `snapback4/crates/snapback4/src/serve_maintenance.rs:436`.
